pathlib.Path.glob
Glob the given relative pattern in the directory represented by this path, yielding all matching files (of any kind):

>>> sorted ( Path ( '.' ) . glob ( '*.py' )) [PosixPath('pathlib.py'), PosixPath('setup.py'), PosixPath('test_pathlib.py')] >>> sorted ( Path ( '.' ) . glob ( '*/*.py' )) [PosixPath('docs/conf.py')] >>> sorted ( Path ( '.' ) . glob ( '**/*.py' )) [PosixPath('build/lib/pathlib.py'), PosixPath('docs/conf.py'), PosixPath('pathlib.py')

[S2] chunk_id=pathlib.Path.rglob:0 url=https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path.rglob
pathlib.Path.rglob
Glob the given relative pattern recursively. This is like calling Path.glob() with “ **/ ” added in front of the pattern .

Note

The paths are returned in no particular order. If you need a specific order, sort the results.

Note

Any OSError exceptions raised from scanning the filesystem are suppressed. This includes PermissionError when accessing directories without read permission.

See also

Pattern language and Path.glob() documentation.

[S4] chunk_id=pathlib.PurePath.full_match:0 url=https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.PurePath.full_match
pathlib.PurePath.full_match
Match this path against the provided glob-style pattern. Return True if matching is successful, False otherwise. For example:

>>> PurePath ( 'a/b.py' ) . full_match ( 'a/*.py' ) True >>> PurePath ( 'a/b.py' ) . full_match ( '*.py' ) False >>> PurePath ( '/a/b/c.py' ) . full_match ( '/a/**' ) True >>> PurePath ( '/a/b/c.py' ) . full_match ( '**/*.py' ) True

See also

Pattern language documentation.

As with other methods, case-sensitivity follows platform defaults:

>>> PurePosixPath ( 'b.py' ) . full_match ( '*.PY' ) False >>> PureWindowsPath ( 'b.py' )

[S5] chunk_id=pathlib.PurePath.match:0 url=https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.PurePath.match
pathlib.PurePath.match
Match this path against the provided non-recursive glob-style pattern. Return True if matching is successful, False otherwise.

This method is similar to full_match() , but empty patterns aren’t allowed ( ValueError is raised), the recursive wildcard “ ** ” isn’t supported (it acts like non-recursive “ * ”), and if a relative pattern is provided, then matching is done from the right:

>>> PurePath ( 'a/b.py' ) . match ( '*.py' ) True >>> PurePath ( '/a/b/c.py' ) . match ( 'b/*.py' ) True >>> PurePath ( '/a/b/c.py' ) . match ( 'a/*.py' ) False

Changed in version 3.12: The pattern parameter accepts a path-like object .

Changed in version 3.12: The case_sensitive parameter

Find all .py files anywhere below a folder using a glob pattern.

message.content:
Use `pathlib.Path.rglob()` to find all `.py` files recursively below a folder:

```python
import pathlib

folder = pathlib.Path(".")
py_files = list(folder.rglob("*.py"))
print(py_files)
```

This matches any `.py` file anywhere in the directory tree. Paths are returned in no particular order; sort if needed.
